text:
MPC rose 0.18% today to close at $387.71, capping a strong two-week rally of 8.23%. The gain reflects broad momentum in refining stocks driven by tight energy markets: U.S. crude has climbed more than 9% this week amid escalating Iran-Kuwait military tensions, while U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity with relatively lean inventories of gasoline and diesel. Higher oil prices and full-capacity operations support refiner margins—the spread between what they pay for crude and what they earn selling finished fuel.

The two-week surge also sits within a longer trend of strength for energy stocks as geopolitical risk in the Middle East persists and there's little sign of supply relief. This week's Iran-Kuwait strikes and ongoing U.S.-Iran tensions have kept crude elevated, which, combined with strong refining utilization, creates conditions where refiners convert crude into products more profitably.
